1.why: All 11 screens are static pages with plain cards and buttons; no animation, moving images, or pop-ups appear at any step.

2.why: Large bold headings, solid blue buttons, and green status lines stand out clearly, though the dark Logs panel is equally eye-catching and can pull attention away from the task.

3.why: Persistent labelled tabs and one task card per page make the needed action easy to locate, although Helena must herself realise to switch to 'Enter code' after requesting the reset.

4.why: Each screen states the next action, but the user must still remember a complex 12-character password and carry two separate codes across a long multi-step flow.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill hint, or password-manager affordance is visible on any screen (only bare manual inputs), so such options are not demonstrably present.

6.why: Previously entered values reappear for recognition (her contact email retained in step 2, the reset code prefilled in step 3, the security code prefilled in step 9), though no saved-account or profile recognition aids exist.

7.why: User-facing sentences are short and mostly plain, but phrases like 'email-style contact value' and 'authenticated session' are technical for a 67-year-old reader.

8.why: No error state appears in any screenshot, so whether error messages describe the problem and fix cannot be confirmed; only clear green success messages are shown.

9.why: Helper text states rules ('At least 12 characters...', 'Use an email-style contact value') but no screen shows a concrete example of what to type.

10.why: The system offers no choice between password, code, or face login (it enforces a fixed password-then-code sequence), though the three tab choices that do exist are clearly labelled.

11.why: Every screen presents a single task with one primary button and at most three tabs, so the user is never faced with many choices at once.

12.why: Each action produces an explicit green outcome line plus a Logs entry, although the reset confirmation is deliberately non-committal ('If eligible, reset instructions have been prepared').

13.why: Each new step includes a short tip (codes expire after 15 minutes, password composition rules, mock code shown in the Logs panel), but no further on-demand help is offered.

14.why: Tabs and forms remain available so retrying seems possible, but no failed-attempt screen is shown to demonstrate that recovering from a mistake is easy.

15.why: The header, tabs, card layout, button styles, and Logs panel are identical across all 11 steps, so the design is fully consistent and learnable over time.
